title: Chandrayaan I II
definition: India's pioneering lunar exploration missions conducted by ISRO, with Chandrayaan-1 acting as India's first lunar orbiter and impact probe that confirmed water molecules on the Moon, and Chandrayaan-2 serving as an advanced mission featuring an Orbiter, Lander (Vikram), and Rover (Pragyan) to study lunar topography, mineralogy, and exosphere.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial under Science and Technology (Space Technology, Indigenization of Technology, Space Missions) and International Relations (global space cooperation). Frequently tested in Prelims regarding specific payloads, mission objectives, orbit details, and scientific discoveries. Relevant in Mains for India's scientific capabilities, soft power, and deep-space ambitions.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts, chronology, and technical mechanisms of Chandrayaan-1 and Chandrayaan-2.
Evaluate payloads, scientific objectives, orbital configurations, and findings of both missions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky UPSC Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of satellite orbits, launch vehicles (PSLV and GSLV), and remote sensing technology.
